text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections, have you noticed any passing of small, sand-like particles in your urine or any worsening pain after physical activity? Also, have you ever undergone imaging for your kidneys in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis). Based on your history of recurrent UTIs and the classic presentation of hematuria with unilateral flank pain, you likely have a stone in the right ureter. I will confirm this by ordering a Non-Contrast CT of the Abdomen and Pelvis.
